mainTopic: Where the כהן גדול could sit during the Yom Kippur reading (sitting is banned in the עזרה), the source of רב חסדא's answer, and what 'הגדול' means in עזרא's blessing.
overview: The גמרא asks how the כהן גדול could sit before his יום כיפור reading, since only kings of בית דוד may sit in the עזרה. The answer, based on רב חסדא's statement about the הקהל reading, is that the reading took place in the עזרת נשים. A פסוק about עזרא's public reading leads to the question of what 'the great God' means in his blessing. One view is that עזרא said the שם המפורש. Another explains it as a special wording of praise. Since the שם המפורש is not said outside the מקדש, עזרא's use of it is explained as a הוראת שעה. The גמרא then tells how the people at that gathering prayed to be rid of the יצר הרע for עבודה זרה and sealed it in lead, and how they weakened the יצר for עבירה by blinding it without destroying it. Next comes the version from ארץ ישראל: the אנשי כנסת הגדולה restored 'great, mighty, and awesome' after ירמיה and דניאל had dropped words out of truthfulness. Finally, the גמרא returns to the משנה and asks how the כהן גדול may skip from 'אחרי מות' to 'אך בעשור'. אביי answers that skipping in the Torah is allowed within one topic, and a ברייתא supports him.

steps.title: Nobody may sit in the Temple courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that the כהן גדול was sitting before the reading, since sitting in the עזרה is allowed only for kings of בית דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no sitting in the Temple courtyard except for kings of the House of David alone, as it says: 'King David came and sat before ה׳.' So how could the כהן גדול be sitting?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge. The wording of the משנה implied that the כהן גדול was sitting until the moment he stood to read, and the גמרא asks how that is possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that no one may sit in the עזרה except kings from בית דוד. Its source is the פסוק where דוד המלך 'sat before ה׳.' If the כהן גדול was sitting before the reading, it looks as though he broke this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is stated (introduces a verse)

steps.confusionAlert: The question mark makes this whole line a challenge, not a new ruling. The rule about sitting is quoted as a weapon against the assumption that the כהן גדול was sitting.

phrases.english: There is no sitting in the Temple courtyard
except for kings of the House of David alone.
As it is stated: 'Then King David came'
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א יז:טז

phrases.english: and sat before the Lord'? (So how could the High Priest be sitting?)

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין יְשִׁיבָה בָּעֲזָרָה אֶלָּא לְמַלְכֵי בֵּית דָּוִד בִּלְבַד
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that the כהן גדול was sitting in the Temple before the reading.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sitting in the עזרה is forbidden to everyone except kings of בית דוד, and the כהן גדול is not such a king.

steps.title: The reading was in the women's courtyard
steps.stepSummary: Using רב חסדא's principle, the גמרא answers that the reading took place in the עזרת נשים, where sitting is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חסדא said in another case, 'in the women's courtyard,' here too the reading was in the women's courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by moving the location. The reading was not in the inner עזרה but in the עזרת נשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on sitting applies only to the holier inner courtyard. The עזרת נשים does not have that restriction, so the כהן גדול could sit there. The גמרא borrows this idea from a statement רב חסדא made elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: As [so-and-so] said (borrowing an answer from elsewhere)
The women's courtyard, an outer area of the Temple with less holiness

phrases.english: As Rav Ḥisda said: in the women's courtyard,
here too, it was in the women's courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the case to a place where the rule does not apply
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the reading was in the inner עזרה, where sitting is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reading was in the עזרת נשים, where sitting is allowed.

steps.title: Where did רב חסדא originally say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רב חסדא's 'women's courtyard' statement first appeared and says it was said on the following source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where was the statement of רב חסדא said? On this:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to show the original source where רב חסדא made his statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא has just borrowed רב חסדא's idea, so it now shows the original setting. 'אהא' points forward to the ברייתא quoted in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: On this (pointing to the source that follows)

phrases.english: And where was Rav Ḥisda's statement said?
On this:

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The original context of רב חסדא's statement.

steps.title: The ברייתא about where the הקהל reading took place
steps.stepSummary: In the original setting, a ברייתא was raised as an objection. It says the הקהל reading was in the עזרה, while רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says it was on the הר הבית, based on a פסוק about עזרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected from a ברייתא: Where do they read it (the הקהל reading)? In the courtyard. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: On the Temple Mount, as it says: 'He read from it before the open square that was before the Water Gate.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the original source on which רב חסדא spoke. It is a ברייתא that was brought as a challenge, because the first opinion places the king's sitting-and-reading in the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king reads at הקהל while sitting, so if the reading was in the inner עזרה, that clashes with the 'no sitting' rule. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב places it on the הר הבית, using the פסוק about עזרא reading near the Water Gate.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a תנאי source)
As was taught in a ברייתא
The Temple Mount, outside the courtyards

phrases.english: They raised an objection, as was taught in a baraita:
Where do they read from it (at the assembly)? In the courtyard.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: בְּהַר הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says: On the Temple Mount,
as it is stated: 'And he read from it before the wide square'
phrases.notes: נחמיה ח:ג

phrases.english: that was before the Water Gate.'

steps.kashyaTarget: The king sitting while reading in the עזרה at הקהל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first opinion places the reading in the עזרה, yet sitting there is forbidden except for kings of בית דוד.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the 'courtyard' means the women's courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the 'courtyard' in the ברייתא is the עזרת נשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: in the women's courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: This is רב חסדא's original statement. It explains which courtyard the ברייתא means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'עזרה' in the ברייתא refers to the עזרת נשים, where sitting is allowed, so the objection falls away. This is the same idea the גמרא borrowed in step 2.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's principle is that a public reading 'in the עזרה' means the עזרת נשים, where sitting is permitted. It solves both the הקהל case and the יום כיפור case.

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda said: In the women's courtyard.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'עזרה' means the inner courtyard, where sitting is forbidden.

steps.title: What does 'the great' mean in עזרא's blessing?
steps.stepSummary: Because the ברייתא quoted a פסוק about עזרא's reading, the גמרא now explains a nearby פסוק and asks what 'הגדול' adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And עזרא blessed ה׳, the great God.' What is meant by 'great'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic sparked by the פסוק in נחמיה. It asks what 'great' means here, which sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הגדול' seems to say that עזרא did something special to 'make God great' in his blessing. The גמרא wants to know what that special act was.

phrases.english: 'And Ezra blessed the Lord,'
phrases.notes: נחמיה ח:ו

phrases.english: 'the great God.'
What is meant by 'great'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Prompted by the פסוק from נחמיה quoted in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What act of 'making God great' the word 'הגדול' describes.

steps.title: He made God great with the explicit Name
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף in the name of רב says עזרא 'made Him great' by saying the שם המפורש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said in the name of רב: He made Him great with the explicit Name.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first answer. עזרא honored God by pronouncing His special, explicit Name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שם המפורש is the holiest form of God's Name, said as it is written. Saying it in public would be a special way of declaring God's greatness.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rav said:
That he ascribed greatness to Him with the explicit Name.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Great' means עזרא said the שם המפורש.

steps.title: He made God great with 'from world to world'
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל gives a different answer: the 'greatness' was the phrase 'Blessed is ה׳... from world to world.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said: 'Blessed is ה׳, God of Israel, from world to world.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second answer. רב גידל says עזרא's greatness was the special wording 'from world to world' in the blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב גידל ties 'great' to a wording, not to the Divine Name. The phrase 'מן העולם ועד העולם' praises God as ruling over this world and the next.

keyTerms.meaning: From world to world / from eternity to eternity

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said:
'Blessed be the Lord, God of Israel,'
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א טז:לו

phrases.english: 'from eternity to eternity.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Great' refers to the wording 'from world to world.'

steps.title: Why not say it was the explicit Name?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב דימי why רב גידל does not accept the simpler answer that עזרא used the שם המפורש.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב דימי: But maybe it means he made Him great with the explicit Name?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב גידל's explanation. He asks why we don't just say it was the שם המפורש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer seems natural and fits the word 'great.' אביי wants to know what pushed רב גידל away from it.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Dimi:
But perhaps it means he ascribed greatness to Him with the explicit Name?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב דִּימִי: וְדִילְמָא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The שם המפורש explanation seems simpler, so why reject it?

steps.title: The explicit Name is not said outside the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי answers that the שם המפורש may not be said outside the מקדש, and עזרא's reading was not inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The explicit Name is not said in the outlying areas (outside the Temple).
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי defends רב גידל. עזרא could not have used the שם המפורש because he read outside the מקדש, where saying it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שם המפורש may be said only in the מקדש. עזרא read by the Water Gate square, outside the מקדש. So 'great' must mean something else, like רב גידל's wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Outlying areas: anywhere outside the מקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The שם המפורש may be said only in the מקדש, never בגבולים. That is why רב גידל explains עזרא's 'greatness' as the wording 'from world to world.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic boundary in הלכה on pronouncing the Divine Name and shows how a rule of הלכה can decide how we read a פסוק.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The explicit Name may not be said in the provinces (outside the Temple).

steps.terutzResolutionType: A halachic restriction rules out the alternative reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עזרא may have pronounced the שם המפורש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שם המפורש is forbidden outside the מקדש, so 'great' means the phrase 'from world to world.'

steps.title: Didn't Ezra use God's explicit name outside the Temple?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב דימי's rule. רב גידל said that at עזרא's public reading, which was outside the מקדש, עזרא made God great by saying the שם המפורש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it really not allowed? But the פסוק says: 'And עזרא the scribe stood on a wooden tower that they made for the occasion.' And רב גידל said that עזרא made God great by saying the שם המפורש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the rule from the last step, that the שם המפורש may not be said outside the מקדש. It points to a teaching that עזרא did exactly that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scene with the wooden tower was a public gathering outside the מקדש. רב גידל explains the later words in that passage, 'the great God', to mean that עזרא pronounced the שם המפורש. If that is true, the שם המפורש can be said outside the מקדש, which contradicts רב דימי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And not?' The גמרא doubts a claim that was just made.
'But isn't it written...?' This introduces a פסוק used as a challenge.
God's explicit, special name, pronounced as written.

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק quoted here (about the wooden tower) is only the opening of the passage. The word 'great' that רב גידל explains comes a few פסוקים later: 'and עזרא blessed ה׳, the great God'. The גמרא quotes the opening line to show that this event took place outside the מקדש.

phrases.english: And is it not [allowed]?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is questioning רב דימי's rule from Step 10.

phrases.english: But isn't it written: 'And Ezra the scribe stood'

phrases.aramaic: עַל מִגְדַּל עֵץ אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ לַדָּבָר״.
phrases.english: upon a wooden tower which they made for the purpose.'
phrases.notes: A public gathering in Jerusalem, not inside the מקדש.

phrases.english: And Rav Giddel said:
that he made Him great with the explicit name!
phrases.notes: So the שם המפורש was said outside the מקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of Step 10, that the שם המפורש may not be said outside the מקדש.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's rule that the שם המפורש may not be said outside the מקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching says עזרא used the שם המפורש at a gathering outside the מקדש, so it seems to be allowed there.

steps.title: It was a one-time emergency ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that עזרא's use of the שם המפורש was a הוראת שעה, a special ruling for that moment only.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was a one-time ruling for that hour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. What עזרא did was a special exception for that moment, not the normal rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule stays the same: the שם המפורש is not said outside the מקדש. עזרא's case was a הוראת שעה, a temporary permission given because of that unique moment of the nation's return to God. An exception like this does not set a precedent.

keyTerms.meaning: A one-time, emergency ruling for special circumstances. It is not a permanent law.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא tool. An unusual event in תנ״ך is explained as a הוראת שעה, so it does not overturn the regular הלכה.

phrases.english: It was a provisional ruling for that time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the event was a one-time exception.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עזרא's use of the שם המפורש outside the מקדש shows it is generally allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was a הוראת שעה. The normal ban outside the מקדש still stands.

steps.title: What did the people cry out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to another פסוק from that same gathering, 'they cried out to ה׳ in a loud voice', and asks what they actually said.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they cried out to ה׳ their God in a loud voice.' What did they say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new פסוק from the same event and asks what words the people cried out. This sets up the story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the people cried out loudly but does not tell us their words. The גמרא wants to fill in what their prayer was.

phrases.english: 'And they cried out to the Lord, God'
phrases.notes: From the gathering in נחמיה.

phrases.english: with a loud voice.'
What did they say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the הלכה question and explains a nearby פסוק from the same event.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The actual words of the people's loud cry.

steps.title: The people beg to be rid of the urge for idol worship
steps.stepSummary: רב (or רבי יוחנן) says the people cried 'Woe, woe!' about the יצר הרע for עבודה זרה. It destroyed the מקדש and exiled Israel, and they no longer wanted it or the reward for overcoming it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said, and some say it was רבי יוחנן: 'Woe, woe! It is this one that destroyed the מקדש, burned the היכל, killed all the righteous, and exiled Israel from their land. And it still dances among us! Didn't You give it to us only so we could earn reward for beating it? We don't want it, and we don't want its reward!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers what the people cried out. They begged God to remove the יצר הרע for עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'This one' means the יצר הרע for עבודה זרה. The people list the disasters it caused and complain that it is still active among them. They know it was given so people could earn reward by overcoming it, but they say they would rather give up the reward than keep the danger.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Dances among us.' It is still active among us.
'And some say.' This marks a doubt about who said the teaching.

phrases.english: Rav said, and some say Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Woe, woe! It is this one
phrases.notes: The יצר הרע for עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: that destroyed the Temple
and burned its Sanctuary
and killed all the righteous ones
and exiled Israel from their land,
and it still dances among us.
Did You give it to us
for any reason other than so we could receive reward through it?
We don't want it,
and we don't want its reward!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They cried out against the יצר הרע for עבודה זרה, asking that it be removed even at the cost of losing the reward for overcoming it.

steps.title: A note falls from heaven saying 'Truth'
steps.stepSummary: In response to their prayer, a note fell from heaven with the word 'אמת' written on it, showing that God agreed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A note fell to them from heaven, and on it was written 'אמת' (truth).
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. Heaven answers the people's prayer with a note that says 'אמת'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The note signals that God accepted their request. This sets up the next step, where a lesson is drawn from the word written on it.

keyTerms.meaning: A note or slip of paper.

phrases.english: A note fell to them from heaven,
on which was written 'Truth.'
phrases.notes: A sign that God agreed to their request.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with heaven's response to the prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heaven answered the prayer with a note reading 'אמת'.

steps.title: God's seal is Truth
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא learns from the note that the seal, or signature, of הקדוש ברוך הוא is 'אמת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא said: Learn from this that the seal of הקדוש ברוך הוא is 'אמת'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנינא draws a lesson from the story. Since heaven signed its answer with 'אמת', truth must be God's personal seal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A seal is how a king signs and confirms a document. A heavenly message marked only with 'אמת' shows that truth is God's signature. This is a side lesson that grows out of the story.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Learn from this.' It introduces a lesson drawn from what was just said.

steps.whatToRemember: עזרא's use of the שם המפורש outside the מקדש was only a הוראת שעה. At that gathering the people begged to be freed from the יצר הרע for עבודה זרה, and heaven answered 'אמת', which teaches that God's seal is truth.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥanina said:
Learn from this
that the seal of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is 'Truth.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a lesson from the heavenly note in Step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The seal of הקדוש ברוך הוא is truth (אמת).

steps.title: The fast and the fiery lion cub
steps.stepSummary: After a three-day fast, the יצר הרע for עבודה זרה is handed over to the people. It emerges from the קודש הקדשים like a lion cub of fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sat in a fast for three days and three nights, and it was handed over to them. Something like a lion cub of fire came out of the קודש הקדשים. The נביא said to Israel: This is the יצר for עבודה זרה, as the פסוק says, 'And he said: this is the wicked one.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues from the note of 'אמת'. The people fast, and the יצר הרע for עבודה זרה actually appears in front of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'אמת' note told them Heaven agreed with their prayer, and now the agreement takes effect. The יצר comes out of the קודש הקדשים, the place where it had done the most damage. The word 'זאת' ('this') in the פסוק is read as pointing at something you can physically see.

keyTerms.meaning: the Holy of Holies, the innermost room of the מקדש
the evil inclination for idol worship

phrases.english: They sat in a fast
three days and three nights,
and it was handed over to them.
phrases.notes: 'It' means the יצר הרע for עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: Something like a lion cub of fire came out
from the Holy of Holies.
The prophet said to Israel:
phrases.notes: The prophet here is זכריה.

phrases.english: This is the inclination for idol worship,
as it says: 'And he said: this is the wicked one.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹתִיבוּ בְּתַעֲנִיתָא תְּלָתָא יוֹמִין וּתְלָתָא לֵילָוָאתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the result of the heavenly 'אמת' agreement from Step 15, continuing the prayer of Step 14 (Step 16 was a side remark by רב חנינא).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יצר for עבודה זרה was handed over and appeared physically from the קודש הקדשים.

steps.title: The shriek and the fear of heavenly mercy
steps.stepSummary: When they grab it, a hair falls out and it screams so loudly it is heard 400 פרסאות away. The people worry Heaven will take pity on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they grabbed it, one hair fell from its hair. It let out a cry, and its voice traveled 400 פרסאות. They said: What should we do? Maybe, חס ושלום, Heaven will have mercy on it.
steps.whatsHappening: Catching the יצר creates a new problem. The people ask what to do, which sets up the נביא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Losing just one hair makes the יצר scream. The people fear that if its cries are heard, Heaven may feel pity and undo their victory. So the question is practical: how do they keep it quiet?

phrases.english: When they caught hold of it,
one hair slipped out of its hair
and it let out a cry,
and its voice traveled four hundred parasangs.
They said: What should we do?
Perhaps, Heaven forbid,
they will have mercy on it from Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A problem arises right after the יצר is captured.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can they stop the יצר's cries from bringing it heavenly mercy?

steps.title: Sealing it in a lead pot
steps.stepSummary: The נביא tells them to seal the יצר inside a lead container, because lead absorbs sound. A פסוק in זכריה supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The נביא said to them: Throw it into a pot of lead and cover its opening with lead, because lead absorbs sound. As the פסוק says: 'And he said: this is the wicked one, and he cast it into the ephah, and he cast the stone of lead onto its opening.'
steps.whatsHappening: The נביא answers the question from the last step: lock the יצר in lead so no one can hear it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lead blocks sound, so the cries cannot reach Heaven. The פסוק in זכריה describes a woman called 'wickedness' being thrown into a measuring container and sealed with a lead stone. The גמרא reads that vision as describing this very event.

keyTerms.meaning: a stone, or weight, of lead

phrases.english: The prophet said to them:
Throw it into a pot of lead,
and cover its opening with lead,
since lead absorbs sound.
As it says: 'And he said: this is the wicked one,
and he cast it into the measuring container,

phrases.aramaic: וַיַּשְׁלֵךְ אֶת אֶבֶן הָעוֹפֶרֶת אֶל פִּיהָ״.
phrases.english: and he cast the stone of lead onto its opening.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ נָבִיא: שַׁדְיוּהוּ בְּדוּדָא דַאֲבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Seal the יצר in lead, which absorbs sound, so its cries cannot reach Heaven.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the episode of the יצר for עבודה זרה. It was effectively removed from Israel.

steps.title: Praying to capture the inclination for sin too
steps.stepSummary: Seeing that Heaven is accepting their prayers, they pray about the יצר for עבירה (forbidden relations), and it is also handed over to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Since this is an עת רצון, a favorable time, let us pray about the יצר for עבירה. They prayed, and it was handed over to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The story opens a second episode. Encouraged by their success, the people now ask to capture the יצר for forbidden relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their reasoning is that a moment when Heaven is accepting prayers should be used for more. This time the target is a different יצר, the urge toward עריות. The request works, and that sets up the problem in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: a favorable time, when prayers are accepted
the inclination for sin, here meaning forbidden relations

phrases.english: They said: Since it is a favorable time,
let us pray about the inclination for sin.
They prayed,
and it was handed over into their hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the success with the יצר for עבודה זרה to start a second capture.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יצר for עבירה was also handed over to them.

steps.title: Warning: killing it would end the world
steps.stepSummary: The נביא warns that killing this יצר would destroy the world. They imprison it for three days instead, and not one fresh egg can be found in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: See, if you kill that one, the world will end. They imprisoned it for three days. They searched for a fresh egg in all of ארץ ישראל and could not find one.
steps.whatsHappening: The נביא warns them that this יצר cannot simply be destroyed. Their test of locking it up proves he is right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the יצר for עבודה זרה, this desire is also what drives living things to reproduce. With it locked away, even chickens stopped laying eggs. So wiping it out completely would mean no new life at all.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the desire is good when it leads to sin. It is saying that the same basic drive is needed for life to continue, so it cannot be removed entirely.

phrases.english: He said to them: See,
that if you kill that one,
the world will be destroyed.
They imprisoned it for three days,
and they searched for a fresh egg
throughout all of the Land of Israel, and none was found.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: חֲזוֹ, דְּאִי קָטְלִיתוּ לֵיהּ לְהָהוּא, כָּלֵי עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the danger of the capture from Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יצר for עבירה cannot be destroyed, because it is also the drive behind all reproduction.

steps.title: The dilemma: not all, and not half
steps.stepSummary: They ask what to do. Killing it destroys the world, and asking Heaven to remove only half of it will not work, because Heaven does not give half-gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: What should we do? If we kill it, the world will end. If we pray for half, Heaven does not grant halves.
steps.whatsHappening: The people are stuck and lay out both options, and both fail. This sets up the creative solution in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one, killing it, ends all reproduction. Option two, praying for only half its strength to be removed, fails because Heaven only gives complete gifts. They need some way to weaken it without asking for a 'half'.

phrases.english: They said: What should we do?
If we kill it, the world will be destroyed.
If we pray for half,
Heaven does not grant halves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הֵיכִי נַעֲבֵיד? נִקְטְלֵיהּ כָּלֵי עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the dilemma created by the warning in Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can they weaken the יצר without destroying the world and without asking Heaven for a 'half'?

steps.title: Blinding it and setting it free
steps.stepSummary: They blind the יצר and release it. This works so that people are no longer drawn to their close relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: They blinded its eyes and let it go. This was effective in that a person is no longer aroused toward his close relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the solution to the dilemma and the end of the story. They weaken the יצר themselves instead of asking Heaven for half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blinding the יצר limits its reach without killing it, so the drive for marriage and children stays. The lasting effect is that the urge toward close relatives (עריות of family) was weakened. That is why most people naturally feel no attraction to close family.
steps.whatToRemember: The people at עזרא's gathering fully removed the יצר for עבודה זרה. The יצר for עבירה could only be weakened, not destroyed, because it is also the drive behind all life. The result is that people are not naturally drawn to close relatives.

phrases.english: They blinded its eyes and released it,
and this was effective, so that it does not arouse
a person toward his close relative.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Solves the dilemma of Step 22 and closes the story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The יצר for עבירה was weakened by blinding, not destroyed. As a result, people are not drawn to close relatives.

steps.title: The version taught in ארץ ישראל: what 'great' means
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they taught the debate this way. רב גידל says 'great' means עזרא praised God using the שם המפורש. רב מתנא says it means they said 'the great, the mighty, and the awesome God'.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West (ארץ ישראל) they taught it like this: רב גידל said: 'Great' means that he made Him great by saying the שם המפורש. And רב מתנא said: it means 'the great, the mighty, and the awesome God'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the word 'הגדול' in עזרא's blessing and brings the version of the argument that was taught in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read 'great'. One reading is that עזרא said God's holy name, the שם המפורש. The other is that they brought back the full praise 'great, mighty, and awesome'. The version from ארץ ישראל states who held each view, so the גמרא can now link רב מתנא to another teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
The great, the mighty, and the awesome God

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same debate about 'הגדול' from earlier on the דף (steps 6-8), given here as the version taught in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: In the West they taught it like this:
Rav Giddel said: "Great"
means that he made Him great with the explicit Name,
and Rav Mattana said:
"The great, the mighty, and the awesome God."
phrases.notes: נחמיה ט:לב

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the יצר story and returns to the debate about 'הגדול' in the verse in נחמיה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב גידל reads 'great' as the שם המפורש. רב מתנא reads it as restoring 'great, mighty, and awesome'.

steps.title: רב מתנא's view matches רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב מתנא's view fits a teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי. The אנשי כנסת הגדולה got their name because they returned God's 'crown' to how it used to be.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this view of רב מתנא matches the view of רבי יהושע בן לוי. For רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Why are they called the Men of the Great Assembly? Because they returned the crown to its former glory.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רב מתנא's reading by showing that רבי יהושע בן לוי says the same idea. This step also sets up the story of how the 'crown' was lost and then restored.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'crown' is God's full praise in prayer. If the אנשי כנסת הגדולה restored it, that fits רב מתנא's view that they brought back 'great, mighty, and awesome'. It even explains why they are called 'הגדולה', the 'Great' Assembly.

keyTerms.meaning: The Men of the Great Assembly, the sages at the start of the Second Temple
The crown back to its old glory

phrases.english: And this view of Rav Mattana
matches that of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.
For Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Why are they called by the name
the Men of the Great Assembly?
Because they returned the crown to its former glory.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּרַב מַתְנָא מָטְיָיא לִדְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב מתנא's side of the debate in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: רב מתנא's reading that they restored 'great, mighty, and awesome'
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי's explanation of the name אנשי כנסת הגדולה

steps.title: How the crown was lost: משה, ירמיה, and דניאל
steps.stepSummary: משה praised God as great, mighty, and awesome. ירמיה saw nations partying in the בית המקדש and dropped 'awesome'. דניאל saw the Jews enslaved and dropped 'mighty'.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה came and said: 'The great, the mighty, and the awesome God.' ירמיה came and said: Nations are partying in His Temple; where is His awesomeness? He did not say 'awesome'. דניאל came and said: Nations are enslaving His children; where is His might? He did not say 'mighty'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי tells the history of how God's full praise got shorter over time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each prophet praised God based on what he could actually see in his own time. When the בית המקדש was destroyed, 'awesome' seemed hidden, so ירמיה left it out. In the exile, 'mighty' seemed hidden, so דניאל left it out.

phrases.english: Moses came and said:
"The great, the mighty, and the awesome God."
phrases.notes: דברים י:יז

phrases.english: Jeremiah came and said:
Gentiles are carousing in His sanctuary;
where is His awesomeness?
He did not say "awesome."
phrases.notes: ירמיה לב:יח

phrases.english: Daniel came and said:
Gentiles are enslaving His children;
where is His might?
He did not say "mighty."
phrases.notes: דניאל ט:ד

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what 'the crown' was and how it was lost.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Over time, ירמיה left out 'awesome' and דניאל left out 'mighty'.

steps.title: The Men of the Great Assembly restore 'mighty' and 'awesome'
steps.stepSummary: The אנשי כנסת הגדולה explain that God's might shows in His holding back His anger against the wicked. His awesomeness shows in the fact that the Jewish people survive among the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came and said: On the contrary! This is the greatest show of His might: that He controls His anger by being patient with the wicked. And this is His awesomeness: if not for the awe of the Holy One, Blessed be He, how could one nation survive among all the nations?
steps.whatsHappening: The אנשי כנסת הגדולה flip the question around and put both missing words back into the praise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירמיה and דניאל took the exile as a sign that God's might and awe were hidden. The אנשי כנסת הגדולה say the exile actually shows them. Holding back from punishing right away takes even more strength, and the Jews' survival proves God's awesome protection. This is the 'crown' returned to its old glory.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds back His urge (here, His anger)

steps.whatToRemember: The same events can be seen as hiding God's might or as proving it. The אנשי כנסת הגדולה saw the hidden strength and restored the full praise we say in שמונה עשרה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for why we say 'הָאֵל הַגָּדוֹל הַגִּבּוֹר וְהַנּוֹרָא' in the first blessing of שמונה עשרה.

phrases.english: They came and said:
On the contrary, this is the might of His might:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, so it would read simply "this is His might."

phrases.english: that He conquers His inclination,
in that He shows patience to the wicked.
And these are His awesome deeds:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִלְמָלֵא מוֹרָאוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: for were it not for the awe of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
how could one nation be able
to survive among the nations?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the doubts of ירמיה and דניאל and completes רבי יהושע בן לוי's explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God's might is His patience with the wicked, and His awesomeness is Israel's survival. So both words belong in the praise.

steps.title: How could ירמיה and דניאל change משה's wording?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how these sages could uproot the wording of praise that משה had set up.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Rabbis (ירמיה and דניאל), how could they do this and uproot an enactment that משה had set up?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ירמיה and דניאל for dropping words from the praise that משה established. This step sets up רבי אלעזר's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה is the greatest teacher, and he set the words 'great, mighty, and awesome'. Normally, later prophets would not cancel משה's enactment. So the גמרא wants to know how ירמיה and דניאל were allowed to leave words out.
steps.confusionAlert: 'רבנן' here does not mean the usual unnamed Sages. It refers to ירמיה and דניאל.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, how could they do this
and uproot an enactment that Moses instituted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the behavior of ירמיה and דניאל described in step 26 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decision of ירמיה and דניאל to drop 'awesome' and 'mighty'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Later sages should not cancel משה's set wording of praise for God.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: they would not say something untrue about God
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that since they knew God is truthful, they would not say praise of Him that they did not see as true.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Because they knew that the Holy One, Blessed be He, is truthful, they did not say anything false about Him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר defends ירמיה and דניאל. They left out the words out of honesty, not out of disrespect for משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: God loves truth. Saying 'mighty' or 'awesome' when they could not see it would have felt like flattery or a lie. So their honesty to God came before keeping משה's exact wording.
steps.whatToRemember: Praise of God must be sincere. ירמיה and דניאל only said what they truly saw, and the אנשי כנסת הגדולה restored the words once they showed how those words were still true.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Because they knew of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
that He is truthful,
therefore they did not speak falsely about Him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁיּוֹדְעִין בְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the motive behind their behavior
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like ירמיה and דניאל were cancelling משה's enactment.
steps.terutzMaskana: They changed the wording only out of truthfulness, because they would not praise God with words they could not honestly see.

steps.title: The משנה: the כהן גדול reads two separate sections
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that the כהן גדול reads 'אחרי מות' and 'אך בעשור'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he reads 'After the death' (ויקרא ט״ז) and 'But on the tenth' (ויקרא כ״ג).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה about the כהן גדול's reading on יום כיפור. This is a setup line that prepares the question coming in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אחרי מות' is in ויקרא chapter 16, and 'אך בעשור' is in ויקרא chapter 23. Many chapters sit between them, so the כהן גדול must skip ahead in the scroll. That skipping is what the גמרא will question.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah section in ויקרא 16 describing the יום כיפור service
The Torah section in ויקרא 23 about the laws of יום כיפור
The High Priest, who reads from the Torah on יום כיפור

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the problem is the content of the reading. The only issue is that the two sections are far apart, so reading both means skipping in the Torah scroll.

phrases.english: And he reads 'After the death'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:1

phrases.english: and 'But on the tenth'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:26 — several chapters later

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to the משנה after the aggadic discussion about the אנשי כנסת הגדולה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול reads 'אחרי מות' and then 'אך בעשור', which means skipping between them.

steps.title: Contradiction: you may not skip in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה that says skipping is allowed in נביא but not in the Torah, which seems to clash with our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they raise a contradiction: We skip in the Prophets, but we do not skip in the Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets another משנה (in מגילה) against our משנה. That משנה forbids skipping in the Torah, yet our כהן גדול skips.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in מגילה is general: when reading from the Torah, you do not jump from place to place. Our משנה has the כהן גדול jump from chapter 16 to chapter 23. So the two sources seem to disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they contrasted it' — introduces a source that contradicts the one just quoted
We skip (jump from one section to another while reading)
The books of the Prophets, here meaning the הפטרה reading

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction: We skip in the Prophets,
phrases.notes: משנה in מגילה

phrases.english: but we do not skip in the Torah!
phrases.notes: Seems to clash with the כהן גדול skipping

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the skipping described in the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the כהן גדול reads 'אחרי מות' and then 'אך בעשור'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה in מגילה says skipping is forbidden in the Torah, but our משנה has the כהן גדול skip several chapters.

steps.title: First answer: it depends on how long the translator takes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that skipping is forbidden only if the translator would finish before the reader reaches the new place.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. There (in מגילה, where skipping is forbidden), it is when the skip is so long that the translator finishes first. Here (in our משנה, where it is allowed), it is when the skip is short enough that the translator does not finish first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to fix the contradiction by saying each משנה speaks about a different length of skip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In those days a תורגמן translated each verse into Aramaic out loud. While he translates the last verse, the reader rolls the scroll to the new place. If the rolling takes longer than the translation, the people sit and wait in silence, which is disrespectful to them. So a short skip is fine, and a long skip is not.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult' — opens an answer that settles a contradiction
The translator who said each verse in Aramaic for the people
Long enough that he will stop (finish) first

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the order: the first 'כאן' is the משנה in מגילה (long skip, forbidden). The second 'כאן' is our משנה (short skip, allowed).

phrases.aramaic: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן, בִּכְדֵי שֶׁיַּפְסִיק הַתּוּרְגְּמָן.
phrases.english: It is not difficult: Here, it is a length that the translator will finish first.
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה in מגילה — forbidden

phrases.english: Here, it is a length that the translator will not finish first.
phrases.notes: Refers to our משנה — allowed

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן, בִּכְדֵי שֶׁיַּפְסִיק הַתּוּרְגְּמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא) by the length of the skip
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות seem to argue about whether skipping in the Torah is allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree: a short skip (translator still talking) is allowed; a long skip (people left waiting) is forbidden.

steps.title: The first answer is pushed away: no skipping in the Torah at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the 'translator' measure in that same source applies only to נביא, so in the Torah no skipping is allowed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is taught right there: We skip in the Prophets and not in the Torah. And how far may one skip? As long as the translator does not finish first. This implies that in the Torah, one may not skip at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first answer by quoting the rest of that same source. It shows the translator rule was said only about נביא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source first says 'skip in נביא, not in the Torah', and then asks how much one may skip. That 'how much' question can only be about נביא, since skipping in the Torah was already ruled out. So the translator measure does not make Torah skipping permitted, and the first answer falls.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But it is taught about this very case' — brings the continuation of a source to disprove an answer
'And up to how much?' — asks for a measure or limit
'Not at all, not at all' — completely forbidden

phrases.english: But it is taught concerning it:
phrases.notes: This comes from that very same source, a little further on.

phrases.english: We skip in the Prophets, and we do not skip in the Torah.
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the rule again so we can see what comes right after it.

phrases.english: And up to how much may one skip?
phrases.notes: This question is about נביא only

phrases.english: As long as the translator will not finish first,
phrases.notes: The translator measure — said for נביא

phrases.english: which implies that in the Torah — not at all!
phrases.notes: So the first answer cannot stand

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer given in step 32.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects the first answer (the translator-length distinction) as a way to permit skipping in the Torah.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The translator measure in the source applies only to נביא; for the Torah the source forbids skipping completely, no matter the length.

steps.title: אביי's answer: one topic versus two topics
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that skipping in the Torah is allowed when both sections are about one topic, and forbidden when they are about two different topics.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is not difficult. Here (our משנה), it is one topic. There (in מגילה), it is two topics.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new answer to the contradiction. He divides the cases by the subject of the sections, not by the length of the skip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אחרי מות' and 'אך בעשור' both deal with יום כיפור, so they are one topic, and the listeners do not feel any break. The ban in מגילה is about jumping between sections on different subjects, which would confuse the listeners. So both משניות are true, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: A leading אמורא of Babylonia who gives the final answer here
One topic — both sections deal with the same subject
Two topics — the sections deal with different subjects

steps.whatToRemember: Skipping in the Torah is forbidden in general, but it is allowed when both sections are about the same topic. That is why the כהן גדול may read 'אחרי מות' and then 'אך בעשור', since both are about יום כיפור.
steps.confusionAlert: Note the order flips from step 32: here the first 'כאן' is our משנה (one topic, allowed), and the second 'כאן' is the משנה in מגילה (two topics, forbidden).
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for Torah reading: you may move between places in the scroll only when they share one subject, such as the readings for a holiday.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult:
phrases.notes: A new answer after the first one fell

phrases.english: Here, it is in one topic.
phrases.notes: Our משנה — both readings are about יום כיפור, so allowed

phrases.english: There, it is in two topics.
phrases.notes: The משנה in מגילה — different subjects, so forbidden

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to the contradiction of step 31, after the first answer was rejected in step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא) by subject matter
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the length-based answer failed, it seems skipping in the Torah is always forbidden, which would clash with our משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Skipping within one topic is allowed (our משנה); skipping between two topics is forbidden (משנה in מגילה).

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the one-topic and two-topics distinction
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that skipping in the Torah is allowed within one topic, and in נביא even between two topics. In both cases the skip must be short enough that the תורגמן does not have to stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: one may skip in the Torah within one topic, and in נביא even between two topics. In both cases, only if the gap is short enough that the translator will not have to stop and wait.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says almost exactly what אביי just said. This backs up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said skipping in the Torah is allowed only when both sections are about one topic. This ברייתא says the same thing and adds that in נביא you may skip even between two topics. It also applies the translator measure to both the Torah and נביא ('כאן וכאן'). That fits our משנה, where the כהן גדול skips from 'אחרי מות' to 'אך בעשור', which are about one topic: יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught in a ברייתא (here it brings support)
One may skip (jump from one section to another while reading)
Here and there: in both cases, Torah and נביא
The translator who translated the reading aloud for the people

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'וְהָתַנְיָא' often opens a challenge. Here it does the opposite: it brings support for אביי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical rule: skipping in the Torah reading is limited to the same topic, and in both Torah and נביא the gap must be short.

phrases.english: And it was taught in a baraita:
phrases.notes: Introduces a supporting source

phrases.english: One may skip in the Torah within one topic,
and in the Prophets, even between two topics.
Here and there (in both cases),
only within an amount where the translator will not have to stop.
phrases.notes: The gap must be short enough that rolling to the new place finishes before the translator does

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that supports אביי's one-topic and two-topics distinction from step 34.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's rule: in the Torah, skipping is allowed only within one topic.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'מדלגין בתורה בענין אחד ובנביא בשני ענינין, כאן וכאן בכדי שלא יפסיק התורגמן'.

steps.title: No skipping between books of נביאים, except within the Twelve
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא continues: you may not skip from one book of נביאים to another. Within תרי עשר, which counts as one book, you may skip.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one may not skip from one prophet's book to another prophet's book. Among the Twelve Prophets, however, one may skip.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and adds a new rule about skipping between different books of נביאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though skipping in נביא is easier than in the Torah, there is a limit: you cannot jump from one book of נביאים to another. The exception is תרי עשר. These twelve short books were written together as one scroll, so skipping between them counts as staying inside one book.

keyTerms.meaning: From one book of the Prophets to another
The Twelve (Minor) Prophets, counted as one book

steps.confusionAlert: 'מנביא לנביא' means from one prophet's book to another book. It does not mean from one section to another inside the same book, which is allowed.

phrases.english: But one may not skip from one prophet's book to another prophet's book.
But among the Prophets of the Twelve, one may skip,
phrases.notes: The Twelve count as one book

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with an extra limit on skipping in נביא and an exception for תרי עשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Skipping between separate books of נביאים is forbidden, but within תרי עשר it is allowed because they count as one book.
